slides.0.title: Swartland and Tulbagh
slides.0.subtitle: New wave and old vines
slides.1.title: Swartland terroir and old vines
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Climate
slides.1.highlights.0.content: A hot, dry Mediterranean climate with about 200–500 mm of rain a year, mostly May–October, with Atlantic air cooling the nights
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Soils
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Malmesbury shale in the interior, decomposed granite on the Paardeberg and Kasteelberg, and sandstone or quartzite at higher elevations
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Dryland bush vines
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Unirrigated head-trained old vines (40 to 100-plus years) are naturally low-yielding and make dry, mineral Chenin Blanc; key varieties include Syrah, Mourvèdre, Chenin Blanc, Grenache, Cinsault and Carignan
slides.1.content: The core of the Swartland is dryland old vines on shale and granite.
slides.2.title: The new wave: the Swartland Revolution and SIP
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Background
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The Swartland Cooperative was founded in Malmesbury in 1948 and old-vine fruit mostly went to bulk wine; Spice Route (1997) and Sadie Family (1999) began the shift to fine wine
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The Swartland Revolution
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Held in Riebeek-Kasteel from November 2010 for six editions to 2015; founders were Sadie, Badenhorst, Mullineux and Porseleinberg
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The SIP charter
slides.2.highlights.2.content: 100% Swartland WO fruit; native yeast only; no acidification, reverse osmosis, added tannins, fining agents or water; no more than 25% new European oak; Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc excluded
slides.2.content: SIP rule details differ slightly between sources (yeast nutrients, enzymes); only the core items above are examined.
slides.3.title: Tulbagh
slides.3.highlights.0.title: A mountain-ringed basin
slides.3.highlights.0.content: A District about 120 km north-east of Cape Town (demarcated 1971); vineyards at about 200–600 m ringed by peaks above 1,500 m; day-night range of 15–20°C or more
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The 1969 earthquake
slides.3.highlights.1.content: A magnitude 6.3 earthquake on 29 September 1969 severely damaged the town's historic buildings
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Varieties
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Chenin Blanc is the leading white, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir supply Cap Classique base wines, and Shiraz is the leading red
slides.3.content: Tulbagh is a hot-day, cool-night basin often grouped with the Swartland as the interior of the Coastal Region.
In which year did the Swartland Revolution begin?
Which variety does the SIP charter exclude?
Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc are excluded.
What is the signature soil of the Swartland interior?
Malmesbury shale; the Paardeberg is granite.
